subject: SLA template — uptime/latency exceptions and credit timing

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template — uptime/latency exceptions and credit timing

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo today. We had a couple of follow-ups from Procurement and our Platform team on the proposed SLA. Two items are blockers for our legal review: 1) the uptime target in the template (99.95% vs. our desired 99.9% for the specific region we plan to run in), and 2) the latency commitment — we need clarity on whether the 95th percentile tail is measured per-region or global across all zones.

Operationally, our procurement team needs monthly credit calculations to be pro-rata for partial months (we're onboarding mid-billing-cycle) and would like a faster payout cadence in case of a credit trigger (15 days after confirmation instead of 30).

Can you share a redlined sample or a quick proposal that ties uptime bands to percentage-of-monthly-invoice credits and explains measurement logic? Also if there are carveouts for scheduled maintenance, please enumerate typical notice windows.

Attaching a brief export of our expected traffic pattern for August so you can see the burst characteristics.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Wong
Procurement Manager, Skylark Systems
Attachments: uptime-metrics-export-aug2026.csv

Subject: Re: SLA template — uptime/latency exceptions and credit timing

Sam — appreciate the level of detail. Attached is a first-pass SLA draft that maps uptime bands to monthly credit percentages and clarifies measurement windows. High-level notes:

- Proposal: 99.95% platform-wide standard; for region-scoped deployments we can agree to 99.90% as an exception with a modified credit table.
- Credits: pro-rata calculation for partial months is straightforward (credit = downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month * monthly_invoice_amount). We can commit to issuing credits within 30 days by default; requesting 15 days is possible for enterprise accounts with payment terms — will check with finance/legal.
- Latency SLO: default measurement is per-region 95th percentile for API request-to-first-byte over a 30-day rolling window. We can make it explicit in the template.
- Maintenance: standard carveout for planned maintenance with >=48 hours notice; emergency maintenance with <48 hours will be classed separately and not automatically carved out.

I'm looping Laura (legal) and Marissa (product) to confirm the exact wording and any caps on credits. See attached: SLA-Draft-Skylark-20260913.pdf.

Next step: if this looks close, happy to schedule a 30-minute call to iron out payout timing.

Best,
Alex Martinez

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA template — uptime/latency exceptions and credit timing

Thanks for the ping. Quick legal summary after an initial pass on the draft and the asks:

1) Credit formula: the proposed pro-rata calculation is acceptable, but we should cap credits at 100% of the monthly invoice for any given month.
2) Payout timing: 15-day payout increases cash flow risk to Redwood (we need to reconcile with finance). Proposed compromise: expedite internal review and acknowledge credit within 15 days, payout processed within 30 days unless we agree to defray via invoice adjustment on the next billing cycle. We can offer 15-day payout as an exception if Skylark signs a short invoice assignment addendum (we've done this for strategic customers).
3) Downtime definition: define as sustained unavailability measured by failed request rate above a threshold for a continuous 5-minute window, excluding planned maintenance (>=48h notice) and force majeure.
4) Measurement: per-region 95th is operationally okay; product to confirm how we compute request-to-first-byte and whether internal retries are excluded.

Action items: Marissa to confirm metric definition and whether we can export a verification report monthly. I'll draft the addendum language for expedited payout and the credit cap.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: internal-legal-redlines-20260914.txt

From: Sam Wong <sam.wong@skylark.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@skylark.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template — uptime/latency exceptions and credit timing

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping legal/product. A few notes from our side after reviewing your draft and Laura's summary:

* Skylark accepts the regional exception to 99.90% but we need the credit table to scale more favorably for mid-band outages (e.g., a 0.5% monthly credit for 99.85-99.90 rather than the 0.25% currently in the draft).
* We understand the rationale for a 30-day payout but our finance team requires 15-day settlement on credits to meet their month-end reconciliation. Is Redwood able to commit to invoice adjustments (a negative line item) on the next invoice instead of direct payout? That would meet our timing needs.
* Regarding maintenance carveouts: 48 hours notice is OK for planned work. Can you add a clause that any maintenance announced with >72 hours' notice and scheduled during a <02:00-06:00 local maintenance window will not count against uptime?

If we can get wording for the credit ramp and the invoice-adjustment approach, Procurement is ready to move to redlines and a DocuSign path. If not, they'll escalate to their VP of Procurement.

Appreciate it,
Sam
Sam Wong
Procurement Manager, Skylark Systems

2) Legal (Laura) will produce the expedited-payout addendum language that allows invoice-adjustment (negative line item on next invoice) as a mechanism to meet Skylark's 15-day reconciliation need, subject to a credit cap of 100% monthly invoice and standard payment terms.
3) I'll update the credit table to show the more favorable mid-band ramp (we'll propose the 0.5% for 99.85-99.90 band) and circulate an annotated one-page summary for your procurement team.
4) If the annotated summary and addendum are acceptable, we'll generate a DocuSign-ready redline by EOD Friday and schedule a 30-minute walkthrough early next week.
